title: Finding a part by its part number still works
refs: SV-9160 (INV-06; V1 baseline 55767168; PRD 1.5 s4 part number)
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header click the Search box (it is a BUTTON, data-test-id global_search_trigger, not a typeable field) or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K. Global search opens as a CENTRED MODAL over the page: a text input at the top, then a scope tab strip - All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices - each showing its own result count, then results grouped by type with a count beside each heading (e.g. "Work orders (4)"). Esc closes the modal. NOTE: group headings are SENTENCE case in the build ("Work orders", "Part sales"). If a group shows nothing, click that entity's scope tab to confirm it really is 0 rather than scrolling. Modal behaviour verified on the V2 QA branch sv9160 on 14 September 2026.
1. The part 'ZZAUTOTEST Brake Chamber Kestrel', part number 'ZZT-88-4412', exists AND is stocked (quantity on hand 25).
2. Parts access: Catalog & Inventory - View.
custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type the part number exactly as printed, with its dashes: ZZT-88-4412
3. Read the Parts group.
4. Clear the input and type the same part number with the dashes removed: ZZT884412
5. Read the Parts group again.
custom_expected:
Both forms return the part 'ZZAUTOTEST Brake Chamber Kestrel'.
In V1 a part was searchable by its part number with the dashes and without them - the number was stored twice in the search text for exactly that reason. Typing a part number is the normal way a parts clerk finds a part.
THIS CASE IS EXPECTED TO FAIL ON THE CURRENT BUILD. A controlled experiment on 14 September 2026 found this part IS returned by its description (Kestrel, Brake Chamber) but NOT by its own part number, while a second part created minutes earlier with the same vendor, category and tags behaved the same way - which rules out indexing delay, organization scoping and permissions. If you see exactly that, mark the test FAILED and raise nothing new; it is already reported. If it fails differently, that is a NEW problem - report it. If it PASSES, the fix has shipped - tell the QA lead.
IF THIS FAILS: it is a real V1-to-V2 capability loss. Mark the test Blocked with the exact query you typed and what came back, and flag it - a task ticket goes to the Product Owner to confirm whether the loss is acceptable. Do not raise it as a defect until the PO has ruled, and do not pass the test just because the V2 specification allows the new behaviour.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the V1 behaviour recorded in the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (FetchDataQueryHandler.php:317-331, which folds the catalogue part number into the search text both with and without its dashes). Version 1.5 of the specification (Confluence page 576978945) section 4 explicitly indexes the part number for Parts, and section 7 requires an exact match after normalization - so a part number that returns nothing is a build defect, not a product decision.
Standing Rule 96 makes a V1 capability the default expectation and Standing Rule 58 makes a code-versus-document conflict a PO DECISION ITEM, so this case asserts the V1 behaviour and tells you to record and flag rather than guess.
